recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the abandoned extension names or add redundant prose; use FHIR-32351 as the controlling decision for the R5 base planned-date properties.
issue_request: FHIR-22766 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked for Encounter.period to support marking admission and discharge dates as planned; the approved resolution initially called for plannedStartDate and plannedDischargeDate extensions, with possible promotion to core properties.
initial_application: No source commit directly mentioning FHIR-22766 was found. Jira comments identify commit 748edfcfc0afb39891df4303cbec74996f910276 as the actual property change; the associated implementation commit d5986253162e4b14fff3351f2e591f5678e3f91a applied FHIR-32351 by adding Encounter.plannedStartDate and Encounter.plannedEndDate and renaming Encounter.period to Encounter.actualPeriod.
additional_context: FHIR-32351 explicitly superseded the FHIR-22766 extension approach with non-extension base properties. PA minutes corroborate both the original FHIR-22766 vote and the later FHIR-32351 7-0-0 decision. The combined branch already contains Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-32351 in commit 55b6972198ad1e12d56bfb6615d9df709a4f152b.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope Encounter source defines Encounter.actualPeriod, Encounter.plannedStartDate, and Encounter.plannedEndDate, and searches of current core and extension-pack source did not find an abandoned plannedDischargeDate extension implementation requiring a core edit.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification Encounter issue explicitly superseded the FHIR-22766 extension approach with base Encounter.plannedStartDate and Encounter.plannedEndDate properties, and it is already reconciled on the combined branch.
